title: What factor turns 5 into 20?
text: The denominators are 5 and 20. $$20 = 5 \times 4$$, so the second fraction is the first scaled by 4. The numerator must be scaled by the same factor, or the ratios are not equal. A common mistake is to add 15 to the numerator because the denominator grew by 15. What is $$20 \div 5$$?

title: Scale the numerator by that factor
Worked solution
text: $$\frac{3}{5} = \frac{x}{20}$$ gives $$x = 3 \times 4 = 12$$. Cross-multiplying: $$5x = 60$$, so $$x = 12$$. Common mistake: answering $$x = 15$$ by subtracting the denominators. General rule: in a proportion, both parts of the ratio scale by the same factor. Cross-multiplying is that fact written as $$ad = bc$$ for $$\frac{a}{b} = \frac{c}{d}$$.
